cve_summary: In the Linux kernel before 4.16.4, a double-locking error in drivers/usb/dwc3/gadget.c may potentially cause a deadlock with f_hid.
commit_message:
USB: gadget: f_hid: fix deadlock in f_hidg_write()

In f_hidg_write() the write_spinlock is acquired before calling
usb_ep_queue() which causes a deadlock when dummy_hcd is being used.
This is because dummy_queue() callbacks into f_hidg_req_complete() which
tries to acquire the same spinlock. This is (part of) the backtrace when
the deadlock occurs:

  0xffffffffc06b1410 in f_hidg_req_complete
  0xffffffffc06a590a in usb_gadget_giveback_request
  0xffffffffc06cfff2 in dummy_queue
  0xffffffffc06a4b96 in usb_ep_queue
  0xffffffffc06b1eb6 in f_hidg_write
  0xffffffff8127730b in __vfs_write
  0xffffffff812774d1 in vfs_write
  0xffffffff81277725 in SYSC_write

Fix this by releasing the write_spinlock before calling usb_ep_queue()

Reviewed-by: James Bottomley <James.Bottomley@HansenPartnership.com>
Tested-by: James Bottomley <James.Bottomley@HansenPartnership.com>
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org # 4.11+
Fixes: 749494b6bdbb ("usb: gadget: f_hid: fix: Move IN request allocation to set_alt()")
Signed-off-by: Radoslav Gerganov <rgerganov@vmware.com>
Signed-off-by: Felipe Balbi <felipe.balbi@linux.intel.com>
docstring:
"""
Summary: 
Handles writing data to a HID (Human Interface Device) gadget.

Parameters: 
file (struct file *): Pointer to the file structure representing the device.
buffer (const char __user *): Pointer to the user buffer containing data to write.
count (size_t): Number of bytes to write from the buffer.
offp (loff_t *): Pointer to the file offset.

Returns: 
ssize_t: The number of bytes written on success, or a negative error code on failure.

Logic: 
The function first checks if the user buffer is accessible. It then acquires a spinlock to manage concurrent access to the write queue. If a write is pending, it waits until the condition allows for a new write. It copies data from the user buffer to a request structure and queues it for transmission over USB. If the request cannot be queued, it logs an error and releases the write pending state. Finally, it wakes up any waiting processes on the write queue.
"""
